minutes.headline: Sewer Commission backed spending remaining FY23 capital funds on pump station repairs and manholes, and will hold a hearing on a noncompliant property.
minutes.summary: The commission heard from the operations contractor and the business manager on a capital plan for pump stations (cranes, seals, dialers, block heaters, rebuild kits), and agreed to spend remaining FY23 funds including reallocated engineering money on manhole infiltration repairs. Also covered: the Q4 commitment, the town meeting presentation, a hearing on a noncompliant property with grease issues, school grease trap reports, and the Leominster IMA meeting. Minutes of 4/25 were accepted and the meeting adjourned by roll call.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission reached consensus to proceed with the FY23 capital plan for pump station repairs and to get quotes so work is done or encumbered by June 30.
The commission agreed to put available budget money, including unspent engineering funds, toward manhole infiltration repairs.
The commission agreed the business manager should schedule a hearing on a noncompliant property at the next meeting.
The Q4 sewer billing commitment was reported and needs commissioner signatures.
The chair will follow up with the town manager's office about a delayed RFP review, and the 4/25 minutes were approved.

why_it_matters: Sewer capital money not spent or encumbered by June 30 is at risk, so these repairs and the move of engineering funds to manholes shape what sewer ratepayers get for this year's budget.
The noncompliant property has an unpaid balance and no lien is possible, so a hearing is the route the commission has for enforcing grease rules.
watch_next: The hearing on the noncompliant property, to be scheduled for the commission's next meeting.
The delayed RFP review, which the chair will raise with the town manager's office, and the operations contract that expires early next year.
